deficiencies.description: The rewrite adds an unsourced link by stating that the slice through a tumour 'illustrates this' (referring to biologists explanting tumours), whereas the lecturer introduced the slice and stain as an observation of tumour morphology without asserting that it illustrates explantation.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: often they will explant the tumor. Here you're looking at a slice through a tumor and a stain to look at the morphology.

considerations.sourcePassage: Whoops, I forgot to start my clock. Okay.
considerations.reason: Omitted as allowed conversational filler and remark about the lecture.

considerations.sourcePassage: Primary cells really don't grow in culture.
considerations.reason: The word 'really' is used here as an intensifier rather than a scientific hedge, so its omission in 'Primary cells do not grow in culture' does not constitute an unhedged distortion.

considerations.sourcePassage: If you just take any cells out of your body and you disaggregate some of your tissue and throw it into a plastic tissue culture dish, most of those cells, in fact, all of those cells will not grow.
considerations.reason: Converting the lecturer's informal second-person phrasing into formal passive textbook prose is an allowed stylistic change.

considerations.sourcePassage: with regard to the contributions of things like the stroma and other things.
considerations.reason: Rendering 'other things' as 'other components' preserves the original meaning and is an allowed stylistic change.
